identity.name: Weekender
identity.one_liner: The $40 quartz field watch with the Indiglo backlight — the most-sold affordable watch in North America and the one most-cited as a first watch.

narrative.story: The Weekender (2011) is the watch that re-established Timex as a volume player in the 2010s. The 38mm brass case, the interchangeable slip-thru strap, and the Indiglo backlight (Timex's 1992 electroluminescent technology) are the core specification. The Weekender is sold in hundreds of dial/strap colorways and is the most-sold affordable watch in North America. It is the watch most-cited as a first watch — the one a non-collector buys and the one a collector cites when they want a beater that costs less than a meal.
narrative.collector_notes: The Weekender's ticking is audible — the quartz module ticks once per second. The brass case is not stainless; it scratches and patinas. Indiglo is a Timex patent.
